html:
The Grand Duchy of Tuscany was a state in central Italy, with its capital at Florence, from 1569 to 1860. It is on the map from 1650 to 1815.

The Medici, Florence's banking family, became dukes in the 1530s. Cosimo I conquered Siena in the 1550s, and in 1569 the pope made him grand duke. The Medici built Livorno into a free port open to merchants of every faith, and Cosimo II made Galileo his court mathematician.

The Medici line ended in 1737, and Tuscany went to Francis Stephen of Lorraine, husband of Maria Theresa of Austria. His son Peter Leopold, later the emperor Leopold II, ran a reforming government and in 1786 abolished the death penalty, among the first states in the world to do so.

Under Napoleon it became the Kingdom of Etruria and then part of France. Restored in 1814, it voted in 1860 to join Piedmont-Sardinia, and Florence was briefly the capital of Italy.
sum: The Grand Duchy of Tuscany was a state in central Italy, with its capital at Florence, from 1569 to 1860. It is on the map from 1650 to 1815.
